Kills matching fddev, fdctl, firedancer, and firedancer-dev processes by scanning /proc.

# Purpose
This file defines the `kill` configuration stage for a command-line tool. Its purpose is to scan `/proc` for running processes that match Firedancer-related names or that hold Firedancer workspace resources open, then terminate them with `SIGKILL`. The stage also declares the required permission check in [`init_perm`](<#init_perm>), which requests root access to inspect open file descriptors under `/proc/`.

The main logic is in [`init`](<#init>) and [`maybe_kill`](<#maybe_kill>). [`init`](<#init>) walks all process IDs in `/proc`, skips the current process, and calls [`maybe_kill`](<#maybe_kill>) for each one. [`maybe_kill`](<#maybe_kill>) reads `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, `/proc/<pid>/maps`, and `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps` to detect `fddev`, `fdctl`, `firedancer`, and `firedancer-dev`, as well as processes that map the configured huge page mount paths or anonymous huge pages. When it sends `SIGKILL`, it records the PID and later waits for the kernel to remove the process entry with [`wait_dead`](<#wait_dead>) to avoid a race after the signal. The file ends by exporting `fd_cfg_stage_kill`, which registers this stage in the configuration system and marks it as always recreated.
